brief: Lane mb: continuous batching for the hybrid Qwen3.6-35B-A3B (GatedDeltaNet + MoE) on Metal (endor), each sequence's output bitwise identical to solo. Stages: Metal R0 G-B row-exactness tests for every decode kernel at M = 1..8 (rows_exact only for kernels that pass; row-exact variants where cheap); bring-up with G-C (batched logits == solo, N = 2..cap, 130 steps), batched engine == LocalEngine incl. prompts > 2048 tokens, dense batch_metal gate, no-op with batching off (plan show + 256 greedy ids, Qwen3-8B and 35B); localeval aggregate decode tok/s at 1/4/8 streams through intarsia serve. MoE decode at T > 1 de-duplicates expert reads across rows like vLLM while staying bitwise. Hard stop 2026-10-24 12:00 EDT.
hypothesis: Metal's decode GEMVs for fp8 and nvfp4 are row-exact by construction (same per-row K order whatever the unroll), so the multi-row shaders can be registered rows_exact after a G-B test; the MoE needs one new expert-grouped kernel. Batching the shared projections, router and experts should lift 4- and 8-stream aggregate decode well above the 78 tok/s that serial serving gives, at the cost of the per-row GDN and attention launches.

summary: Hybrid continuous batching works on Metal for the 35B at --max-batch 2..8: every decode row is bitwise the solo step (4,550 row-steps over N=2..8, engine == LocalEngine incl. 16k prompts), G-B passes for all decode kernels with three new rows_exact registrations (fp8 and nvfp4 GEMV reuse the multi-row shaders, a new expert-grouped MoE kernel reads each expert once per step), and batching off is a byte-identical no-op. Aggregate decode through intarsia serve rises from 78.5 / 78.4 (4 / 8 streams, 128 generated, serial serving) to 101.3 / 107.5, and from 106.6 / 105.8 to 158.4 / 173.7 with 512 generated; single stream costs about 1%. The expert de-duplication is bitwise but not faster than serial MoE calls on random routing; the step grows 3.8 ms per extra row because the GDN and attention kernels still launch once per row.
lessons: Metal's fp8 and nvfp4 decode GEMVs were already row-exact by construction (per-row K order is lane + 32n whatever UN and RS are), so G-B passed first time; the work was registration, a K = 4096 instantiation and the test.

A sort pass (moe_group, one threadgroup with a serial prefix loop) costs more than expert de-duplication saves at 8 tokens; a per-pair leader scan with one simd ballot per 32 ids has no extra pass. De-duplication only paid when tokens share experts (1.08x at T=8, 0.81x on random routing) and did not change the end-to-end step.
Timing a kernel by repeating one routing measures a warm cache: cycle many routings per measurement.

Short-output localeval cells are prefill-bound for batched serving (0.6 s of serialized prefill per 1k-token prompt): 128 generated tokens show 101 / 108, 512 show 158 / 174, the decode-only rate is 196 / 224.

On Metal busy chunk 64 gave the same tokens as chunk 2048 on the 35B (CUDA diverged at 1024); bitwise chunk invariance at the logits level is untested, so the default stays the solo chunk, and 2048 is also faster than 256 here (101.3 vs 93.5 at 4 streams).
Next lever: the per-row GDN conv / delta-rule and attention launches (about 3.8 ms per extra row): a row axis in those kernels is bitwise by construction and needs one G-B test.
